clue.text: Making a noise and causing annoyance

definitions.meaning: clattering or knocking sounds, like loose parts in a car
unsettling or unnerving someone, as a heckler does a speaker

explanation.surface: Someone is being loud and getting on everyone's nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both clattering noisily and, informally, unsettling or flustering a person.

clue.text: Sound axiom for retaining a good man

indicators.note: retaining means the axiom word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a rule is a principle or axiom
ST, saint, is the crossword shorthand for a good man

explanation.surface: A sensible principle about keeping a decent person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for retaining' puts ST inside RULE. 'Sound' looks like 'sensible' but is the noun for a soft noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustle is a soft crackling noise, like leaves or paper.

clue.text: Recording the head doing an impersonation

indicators.note: the head of the word the is its first letter

parts.note: aping is mimicking someone

explanation.surface: A head teacher is filmed mimicking someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Taping means capturing sound or images on tape, a way of recording.

clue.text: Yet some think this a peerless ground!

definitions.text: Yet some think this a peerless ground!

parts.words: Yet some think this a peerless ground!
parts.note: peerless seems to mean unrivalled, but here means without ..., ironic for a ground named after them

explanation.surface: Fans hail a famous stadium as the best there is.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is London's famous cricket ground; peers sit in the House of Lords, so 'peerless' ironically means lacking peers.
explanation.definitionFit: The great London cricket venue bears a name that also means noblemen.

clue.text: Change in rates with more unpleasant outcome

indicators.note: change tells us to reorder the letters of in rates

explanation.surface: Interest rates shift, leaving people worse off.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastier is the comparative of nasty, meaning more disagreeable.

clue.text: Writing to give tips maybe about credit

indicators.note: about tells us the scrambled letters go round the abbreviation for credit
maybe suggests the word tips is only one possible arrangement of its letters

parts.note: CR is the standard accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: Advice on gratuities given in writing, with a note about credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' turns TIPS into SIPT; 'about' puts that round CR, giving S-CR-IPT.
explanation.definitionFit: A script is handwriting or a written text, so it is a kind of writing.

clue.text: Bovine writer's crib?

parts.note: bovine animals are cattle
a pen is a writer's tool

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a writer has a cow-like way of copying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crib' looks like plagiarising, but it means an animal stall.
explanation.definitionFit: A crib is a manger or stall, an enclosure for livestock.

clue.text: Sense hesitation in a foreign dealer

parts.note: import is meaning or significance
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A trader abroad senses doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: An importer trades in goods brought from overseas, so a merchant handling foreign wares.

clue.text: Cross right back to the SE state first

indicators.note: first says the word for state comes before the compass point
back says the letters for right are turned round

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
SE is the abbreviation for south-east

explanation.surface: A traveller heads back to a south-eastern state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RT into TR; 'first' puts AVER ahead of SE.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel across something.

clue.text: Have a late meal with newsmen and check

parts.note: to sup is to eat supper, the evening meal
the press collectively means journalists

explanation.surface: Someone dines late with reporters and keeps them in line.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to hold it back or quell it, a synonym.

clue.text: More land — perfect!

parts.note: Thomas More wrote of an imaginary island with an ideal society; the surface reads like a farmer delighted with extra acreage

explanation.surface: A landowner is thrilled to gain extra acres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' is capitalised to disguise Sir Thomas More, the Tudor author of the 1516 book about an ideal commonwealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More's imagined island gave its name to any ideal, perfect society.

clue.text: Some of those remaining will get dry

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of what is left over will dry out.
explanation.definitionFit: Sere means withered or parched, a poetic word for dry.

clue.text: A lack of good grounding was responsible for this slip

definitions.text: A lack of good grounding was responsible for this slip

parts.words: A lack of good grounding was responsible for this slip
parts.note: reads like an excuse for an error by someone poorly taught, but literally describes earth giving way down a slope

explanation.surface: A mistake is blamed on poor basic education.
explanation.definitionFit: When unstable ground gives way, earth and rock slide down a hillside in a collapse.

clue.text: Left near-ruined in Northern Ireland

indicators.note: ruined suggests the word near is wrecked and its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Something was abandoned, almost destroyed, in Ulster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' scrambles NEAR into ARNE. Larne is a port town in County Antrim, so the definition is a place in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Larne is a harbour town on the County Antrim coast, a place located in Northern Ireland.

clue.text: A boom? Dispute that

definitions.meaning: a boom is a pole or ... used on a ship's rigging
to argue or box lightly with someone

explanation.surface: Someone questions whether there is an economic upturn.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's boom is a type of pole, and arguing is quarrelling playfully as boxers do in practice.

clue.text: Rendered intoxicated

definitions.meaning: coated a wall with a layer of plaster or render

explanation.surface: Someone was made drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Walls coated in plaster are rendered, and slang for very drunk uses the same word.

clue.text: Not slow to give voice

definitions.meaning: fast, as an ... train or delivery is
to put feelings or thoughts into words

explanation.surface: A speaker is urged to speak up quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: An express service is a fast one, and to state one's views is to utter them.

clue.text: Artistic work it's cheap to reproduce

indicators.note: reproducing the letters of it's cheap means making them anew in another order

explanation.surface: A piece of art is inexpensive to copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastiche is a work imitating another artist's style.

clue.text: A game girl

explanation.surface: A plucky young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitaire card games go by this name in Britain, and it is also a woman's given name.

clue.text: Being mad at an arrangement that's inflexible

indicators.note: an arrangement signals that the letters of mad at an are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about a fixed plan they cannot change.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who will not be moved from a position is unyielding, a synonym.

clue.text: Drink like a fish

parts.note: the idiom means to drink alcohol heavily and habitually

explanation.surface: Someone boozes heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: Tope is also a kind of small shark, which gives the phrase an extra twist.
explanation.definitionFit: To tope is an old verb for drinking alcohol to excess.

clue.text: Security devices good buy for retirement

indicators.note: retirement suggests going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a snip is a bargain, something cheap

explanation.surface: Locks or alarms are a bargain for pensioners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for retirement' turns SNIP round to give PINS; SNIP is British slang for a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: PINs and pins both secure things: number codes at cash machines, or fasteners holding things in place.

clue.text: Warning must be clear if turning in harbour

indicators.note: in says the turned word goes inside the harbour word

parts.note: a port is a harbour

indicators.note: turning says the word for clear is read in the other direction

parts.note: net means clear of deductions, as net profit

explanation.surface: A warning about profits made in a port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes NET into TEN; 'in' puts TEN inside PORT.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent is an omen or sign of something to come, often bad.

clue.text: Delay holding party on a lake in Russia

indicators.note: holding says the delay word contains the party word

parts.note: a lag is a delay
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A celebration is postponed on a Russian lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts DO inside LAG to give LADOG; then add A. Ladoga, near St Petersburg, is Europe's largest lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladoga is the large freshwater lake north-east of St Petersburg.

clue.text: Saw the male sovereign into bed

indicators.note: into says the pieces go inside the word bed

parts.note: taken as written
he is the male pronoun
a sovereign is a pound coin, and L stands for pound

explanation.surface: A king is seen getting into bed.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is a gold coin worth one pound; L (from Latin libra) abbreviates pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Beheld is the past tense of behold, meaning looked at.

clue.text: Oliver the screw

definitions.meaning: Oliver is the title orphan of the Dickens novel
a screw is a turning movement

explanation.surface: Someone named Oliver is called a nasty jailer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screw' is British slang for a prison guard, which the surface exploits.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's orphan carries this surname, and a screw is a turn or contortion.

clue.text: How odd, to prefer a bore!

indicators.note: an odd arrangement of the letters of to prefer a is wanted

explanation.surface: Someone is baffled that anyone would favour a tedious person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a dull person but is the verb meaning to drill a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: To bore is to make a hole through something, which is to pierce it.

clue.text: Again and again concerning "X"

parts.note: of can mean about or concerning
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Repeatedly someone talks about an unknown quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Often means frequently, happening repeatedly.

clue.text: Against beginning concerts traditionally

indicators.note: only the opening letters of the two following words are kept, so their tails are dropped

explanation.surface: Someone objects to concerts starting as they always have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning' keeps the first three letters of each word: CON from concerts and TRA from traditionally.
explanation.definitionFit: Contra is Latin-derived for opposing, as in pros and cons.

clue.text: Stick up for people in holiday accommodation

definitions.text: Stick up for people in holiday accommodation

parts.words: Stick up for people in holiday accommodation
parts.note: reads as defending holidaymakers, but literally describes a rod that holds up campers' canvas shelter

explanation.surface: Someone defends guests at a holiday resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Campers' canvas shelters are held up by upright rods, the stick in question.

clue.text: I object to return of aims to effect reforms

indicators.note: return means the word given by I object is read backwards

parts.note: the object form of I is me
ends are goals or aims

explanation.surface: Someone protests that changes are being made to their goals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns ME into EM before ENDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to correct or improve a text, i.e. to make reforms to it.

clue.text: Sort of tree to stick in the ground?

definitions.meaning: a tree grown on a single upright stem, as gardeners describe
a flagpole or upright post planted in earth

explanation.surface: Someone wonders which tree to plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners call a single-stemmed tree this, and the word also means an upright pole bearing a flag.
